meta.dataset: CET add-on acquisition target screen (New England electrical, solar, controls, utility, generator, W/WW I&C)

platform.name: Commonwealth Electrical Technologies (CET)
platform.constraint: No NYC expansion; New England footprint only

meta.method: Pulled the target universe from ZoomInfo search_companies for private companies with 25-400 employees headquartered in the six New England states. Keyword passes covered electrical contractors, solar, SCADA, substation, generator and building automation. We checked each candidate's ownership, founding year and capabilities against its own website and public sources (press releases, BBB/Blue Book, PrivSource, sponsor sites). Companies owned by PE firms or strategic buyers were moved to meta.pe_backed_competitors. Each target is scored 0-100: capability 30, geography 30 (distance to the nearest CET node, with credit for CT sites near Horton), scale 20, ownership readiness 20.

zoominfo_query_parameters.userIntent: M&A add-on target screening for a PE-backed electrical contractor platform

zoominfo_query_parameters.companyDescription: generator sales service standby power systems

zoominfo_query_parameters.result: Failed - subscription enrichment limit exceeded; revenue/employee figures come from search_companies results

sources_summary: Pfingsten, Mason Wells, Ridgemont, MYR Group, Stark Tech, BaseRock sponsor/advisor pages
Better Business Bureau, The Blue Book ProView, Procore network profiles
Hartford Business Journal, Mainebiz, Providence Business News, Canton Citizen
Boston NECA directory, IBEW Local 103 contractor directory
caveats: Revenue is ZoomInfo's modeled estimate, not reported financials. Several figures look inconsistent with headcount (JM Electrical, Dinto, Rossi, Aldon) and need diligence.
ZoomInfo enrich_companies was blocked by a subscription limit. Founded year, ownership and HQ details come from websites and public sources and are null where they could not be verified.
Ownership is 'unknown' when no public source confirms founder, family or ESOP status. A quiet sale to a sponsor or strategic buyer cannot be ruled out without outreach.

Lat/lon are approximate city centroids (geo_precision 'city'). Distances are straight-line miles to Worcester, Taunton or Norwell. Horton's CT town was not geocoded, so CT sites get a qualitative geography credit.
The web-search quota ran out mid-screen. Later candidates were checked against their company websites only.
Sub-$8M revenue firms (Lighthouse, Universal, Racette, Cole, Cummings) are included as capability tuck-ins and flagged.
Smith + Howard has been exited (sold to TPG Growth) and is excluded. No targets are built for it.

Verified 2026-09-24: sampled 23, confirmed 20, removed 1 (cet-t22 SEMAC: BBB lists it as believed out of business, website unreachable, incorporated 1969 not 1946). Corrected cet-t02 (website/sources to https), cet-t16 (founded 1954; ownership downgraded to unknown - unsupported family reacquisition claim), cet-t25 (sale closed Dec 2021), cet-t38 (specialties per website).

scoring_rubric.capability: 0-30: overlap/extension of CET lines (electrical, solar O&M, EV, energy efficiency) and Horton niches (W/WW, pump stations, generators, utility)
scoring_rubric.geography: 0-30: straight-line distance to nearest CET node; CT sites credited for Horton adjacency; NY exposure penalized
scoring_rubric.scale: 0-20: employees/revenue relative to 25-400 employees and $8-120M band
scoring_rubric.ownership_readiness: 0-20: founder/family ownership, generational succession signals; penalized for recent sales, WBE status or acquirer posture
